A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, exhaustive enumeration of optimal scorers, neural-model experiments, and Banking and MSLR results in Section 7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic and MSLR results, reports revised Banking experiments, and adds HelpSteer evaluation in Section 7, with supplementary results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The loss-aggregation and label-aggregation objectives, sum/product aggregation choices, and principal scoring procedures are retained. Nonuniform label aggregation already appears in v1's formulation and Theorem C.1; v2's Appendix D further analyzes it. The Banking model replacement concerns experimental settings rather than a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds HelpSteer prompt-response ranking, extending evaluation to LLM response attributes. Figure 4 pairs coherence with complexity, verbosity, helpfulness, and correctness. Synthetic, Banking, MSLR, and MS MARCO coverage remains; the synthetic training experiment is relocated rather than removed.

E2.justification: The MSLR comparison loses the unequal-weight loss-aggregation variants (10,1) and (10,50) shown in v1 Table 6. v2 Table 4 retains the equal-weight comparison, now labeled AUCLoA, together with label aggregation and the two single-label objectives.

E3.justification: Banking changes from BERT over serialized features, trained for 10 epochs with hinge loss at a fixed 90% mortgage-positive proportion, to a linear model on numerical features trained with Adam for 100 epochs using logistic loss across multiple proportions. HelpSteer introduces maximum-rating binarization and coherence-based label pairing. Diff/Min AUC reporting expands. Appendix G.3 also replaces the synthetic generator's shared gamma scale with separate alpha/tau symbols; this reported formula revision does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Banking sensitivity sweep over mortgage-label prevalence in Figure 3 and a per-label breakdown of the synthetic Bayes-optimal experiment in Figure 6. Conversely, removing the unequal-weight MSLR rows reduces weight-sensitivity evidence. The existing synthetic skewness study, training experiment, and exhaustive-enumeration analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. v2 explicitly averages Banking results over 25 trials, adds plus/minus values in Table 3 and shaded bands in Figure 3, and displays HelpSteer error bars. The uncertainty quantities and HelpSteer repetition count are unspecified; an increase from a known v1 run count cannot be established.

E6.justification: Banking results are replaced under changed settings: v1 Table 5 reports label/loss aggregation AUCs of (0.64, 0.56)/(0.62, 0.55), whereas v2 Table 3 reports (0.616, 0.562)/(0.626, 0.555). Thus the later result favors label aggregation on minimum AUC, not both labels; this is not a same-setting performance change. v2 also adds HelpSteer and Banking-sweep outcomes and synthetic per-label curves. Figure 2's plotted values change, while the relocated synthetic training table and retained MSLR per-label values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 expands Lemma A.2's proof with explicit pairwise/difference objectives and a necessity argument. Appendix D adds derivations for correlated labels and nonuniform aggregation weights, including the perfectly anti-correlated degeneracy. The principal propositions, counterexample, and Appendix C asymptotic theorem and bound are retained.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution lists, and conclusions retain the same central claims: characterize Bayes-optimal aggregation scorers, establish suitable Pareto-optimality results, and demonstrate possible label dictatorship under loss aggregation. v2 explicitly describes the work as analysis of existing methods, clarifying its existing scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands qualifications and interpretation. Section 5.3 and Appendix F distinguish marginal imbalance from conditional signal quality; Appendix D identifies failure when perfectly anti-correlated labels make the aggregate constant. Section 7 explains why a small AUC gap alone is insufficient. Banking interpretation changes from Pareto dominance to better minimum AUC, and Appendix E develops additional application scenarios.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented Banking features, architecture, optimizer, loss, and training duration, and supplies HelpSteer preprocessing and label-pairing instructions. Table 5 newly states that MS MARCO documents follow their original dataset order. Existing synthetic MLP specifications and prompts are retained after relocation; substantial HelpSteer training details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting HelpSteer, class imbalance, fairness and worst-group evaluation, and applications in retrieval, recommendation, and advertising. The related-work categories and central positioning relative to multi-objective and multi-label ranking remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, motivating examples, scorer comparisons, and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. v2 creates Section 5.3, restructures Section 7, moves synthetic training results into Appendix G.5, and inserts Appendices D–F before the renamed empirical appendix. These changes extend beyond accompanying new experimental content.

P2.justification: v2 merges the two MS MARCO example tables into one, omitting the low-relevance/low-engagement examples. It adds Banking, HelpSteer, and synthetic per-label plots; expands performance tables with Diff/Min AUC columns, direction arrows, and shading; and changes figure sizing and captions. The synthetic training table and exhaustive-enumeration figure are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more informative validation through HelpSteer, the Banking prevalence sweep, repeated-trial reporting, and absolute per-label results alongside AUC gaps. Its explicit anti-correlation limitation and distinction between imbalance and signal quality also improve qualification of the conclusions. These benefits are tempered by removal of unequal-weight MSLR comparisons and incomplete HelpSteer and uncertainty specifications. The net gain is supported but limited; the revised Banking scores do not establish improved performance under the earlier settings.
